# Active Lesson Contract — graph projection

Task: example:mission-control-work-handoff
Projection owner: existing Active Lesson Contract lifecycle
Evidence must establish every operative source clause at its behavior's boundary; reject the substitutes below.
C permits N/A only with a bound reason; I requires independent review; L# supplies carry-through/repair.
Full acceptance evidence, source hashes and authority are retained in structured selected_rules.

## Active lessons

### uda.active-contract.boundary-binding @ r1 (patterns/task-time-lesson-activation.md)

An instruction is satisfied only where its required effect must exist. Reading, understanding, planning, simulating, or mentioning it elsewhere does not discharge the obligation. This extends the existing Active Lesson Contract; do not create a second parallel ledger.

- bind-obligation-to-destination: reasoning -> active-lesson-contract [semantic; L1]
  Do: Bind each active obligation to its actual actor, phase, destination, acceptance evidence, non-substitutes, carry-through, repair, and enforcement mode in the existing Active Lesson Contract.
  Reject: rule ID only; statement that the rule was considered; plan-only evidence

### uda.bootstrap.live-root @ r3 (AGENTS.md)

When current owner instructions require the canonical GitHub bootstrap, **re-fetch the live default-branch root `AGENTS.md` on every user turn before task reasoning, artifact composition, task execution, or answering**.

Tool discovery, current-clock checks, and the bootstrap retrieval itself are permitted prerequisites.

A prior-turn fetch, cached copy, remembered summary, or earlier reasoning does not satisfy per-turn activation.

- live-root-refetch: retrieval -> current reasoning/execution turn [semantic; L2]
  Do: Re-fetch the live default-branch root before substantive work each turn.
  Reject: cached root; artifact composition before bootstrap; prior-turn root read

### uda.chat-work.execution-separation @ r1 (patterns/chat-work-execution-routing-threshold.md)

Follow `patterns/chat-work-execution-routing-threshold.md` for Chat-first reasoning,
ordinary GitHub work, bounded execution eligibility, and minimum-sufficient Work
thinking. Chat owns reasoning and ordinary GitHub work; Work/Codex is execution-only;
a Claude session does both.
Before Work, discover deferred Chat tools too. If Chat/RDC can perform the bounded
SSH/VPS/deployment action, keep it in Chat.
When Work is admitted, apply `patterns/work-model-and-effort-routing.md` for the
canonical GPT-6.1 Sol (GPT-6 Sol fallback) / GPT-6 Astra model-and-effort ladder and telemetry contract.
For controlled supervisory routes also apply
`patterns/runtime-chat-work-authority-admission-and-internal-routing.md`.
Worker handoffs follow `patterns/worker-directive-delivery-and-chat-output-budget.md`:
same-turn runnable directive; long operational payloads go to `.md`/text artifacts.
These references preserve the existing rules rather than creating local copies.

- reasoning-stays-in-chat: handoff -> work/codex directive [semantic; L3]
  Do: Chat retains semantic/architectural reasoning; Work/Codex receives only bounded execution residue after current routing/admission.
  Reject: worker self-authored methodology; Work used for routine Chat-owned GitHub reasoning

### uda.continuation.open-outcome @ r1 (patterns/codex-github-operating-system.md)

- If the parent outcome is OPEN and a safe, authorized, executable next action exists, perform it in the current turn. A plan, explanation, saved diagnosis, promise, or list of next steps is not a substitute for that action.

- continue-open-authorized-work: reasoning -> current task frontier [semantic; L4]
  Do: Execute the next safe authorized in-scope action now while the parent owner outcome remains open.
  Reject: diagnostic summary; plan; promise to continue; list of next steps

### uda.continuity.step-checkpoint @ r2 (patterns/context-compaction-resilience.md)

Plan usage limits, like context limits, can end a turn without warning. Never defer saving to a usage threshold.

At each completed step, push the work to the task branch (work-in-progress commits are fine) and update the checkpoint's done, next, and exact next action. A fresh session in any account must be able to resume from durable state alone. The worker that holds the context writes the checkpoint; do not launch a separate helper at the limit to save work.

- Tiny one-shot tasks do not need a dedicated current-state file.

- save-completed-step: persistence -> durable-task-checkpoint [semantic; L5]
  Do: At each completed step, the worker holding the context pushes the work to the task branch and updates done, next and the exact next action in the durable checkpoint, so any account can resume from durable state alone; never wait for a usage threshold or a helper at the limit.
  Reject: a promise to save later; a summary only in chat; local-only work with no push; waiting for a usage threshold; a helper launched at the limit

### uda.continuity.turn-end-handoff @ r2 (patterns/context-compaction-resilience.md)

Before ending a turn on OPEN work, make the durable checkpoint reflect that turn's state and include a one-line resume instruction. Keep owner-private supervisor state that cannot go in a public repository in a private durable store the successor can reach. List anything bound to one account that the successor must recreate, such as scheduled check-ins and memory.

- Tiny one-shot tasks do not need a dedicated current-state file.

- save-turn-end-handoff: final-delivery -> durable-task-checkpoint [semantic; L6]
  Do: Before final delivery on OPEN work, update the durable checkpoint to this turn's state, keep owner-private supervisor state in a private durable store reachable by the successor, include a one-line resume instruction, and list account-bound scheduled check-ins, memory or other items to recreate.
  Reject: a promise to save later; a summary only in chat; a checkpoint from an earlier turn; private state only in the old account; a handoff that omits account-bound items

### uda.final.timestamp @ r8 (AGENTS.md)

For **every assistant turn** governed by this architecture, the **first line of the final user-visible assistant answer MUST be an explicit date-and-time stamp including a timezone or UTC offset**.

This is a final-output contract and a pre-answer invariant, not a task-dependent recommendation.

The timestamp must appear in the final answer/message content delivered to the user on every assistant turn.

A timestamp written only in hidden reasoning, visible thinking/reasoning UI, analysis, tool-call commentary, scratch work, or any intermediate channel **does not satisfy this requirement**.

An earlier timestamp in reasoning or an intermediate step does not satisfy the final-output contract; use the second reading in the final answer.

The final answer opens with the second reading

and says how long the turn took in total.

Before finalizing every assistant turn, perform a literal output check: the first user-visible line of the final answer must match a date + time + timezone/UTC-offset form.

If it does not, prepend the second reading; the check needs no further reading.

Apply it on every turn even for trivial arithmetic, greetings, smoke tests, follow-up acknowledgments, corrections, status updates, or prompts that otherwise warrant a direct one-line answer.

Simple answers, low-effort reasoning, tool avoidance, brevity, and shallow repository reads **must not waive this invariant**.

Treat failure to emit the timestamp as the first line of the final user-visible answer on any assistant turn as an instruction-following failure even when the timestamp appeared during thinking or the underlying task answer is otherwise correct.

- final-first-line-timestamp: final-delivery -> owner-visible-final [mechanical; L7; predicate {"kind":"final_timestamp_first_line"}]
  Do: Deliver and literally check the final first-line timestamp on every turn.
  Reject: timestamp elsewhere in the answer; treating the stamp as a task-dependent suggestion; timestamp only in commentary; timestamp only in hidden reasoning; checking an earlier draft; repair by taking an extra clock reading; omitting the stamp on a one-line answer; brevity used to waive timestamp delivery; correct content treated as compensating for an absent stamp
- final-elapsed-time: final-delivery -> owner-visible-final [mechanical; L2; predicate {"kind":"final_elapsed_time"}]
  Do: Report total elapsed time from both clock readings.
  Reject: first-line timestamp alone; reusing the first intermediate timestamp; opening with the first reading

### uda.kernel.artifact-delivery @ r2 (AGENTS.md)

**Delivery is part of completion.**

When the owner needs to use a file, packet, handoff, protocol, report, generated artifact, or other output, do not make them navigate GitHub branches or repository paths to obtain it.

Before delivering that output, load the delivery-priority, provenance, companion-material, and pre-close usability rules: `patterns/human-readable-operational-references.md` → **Compact rules moved from root `AGENTS.md`**.

- usable-delivery-before-completion: handoff -> owner-required artifact and companion materials [semantic; L2; C]
  Do: Deliver complete usable artifacts before claiming completion.
  Reject: repository path only; naming the delivery pattern without loading it; completion claimed after creation without delivery

### uda.kernel.clock-cadence @ r2 (AGENTS.md)

Two clock readings per turn, no others (owner, 2026-09-30).

First: the message's sent time if the surface shows it, else a read as the turn's first action.

Second: a read right before writing the final answer.

Read with `date -u` in a shell tool, else the current-time tool, else the code tool's clock;

if a read fails or isn't later than the first, use the next one once.

Never compare clocks or read mid-task.

Don't reuse a prior-turn timestamp

or present capture time as hidden provider sent time.

If no clock answers, say so rather than inventing a time.

- first-reading: retrieval -> current reasoning/execution turn [semantic; L2]
  Do: Use visible sent time or a clock read as the first turn action.
  Reject: a later capture presented as message sent time
- two-read-cadence: final-delivery -> owner-visible-final [semantic; L2]
  Do: Use and report the prescribed current-turn clock cadence.
  Reject: an extra mid-task clock read; an earlier task-time reading used as the final reading; clock shopping for a preferred timestamp; a mid-task comparison of clock sources; prior-turn timestamp reuse; fabricated time presented as a reading; repeated retries after the one permitted next read; captured time claimed as hidden provider sent time

### uda.kernel.continuation @ r2 (AGENTS.md)

Before final delivery, apply `patterns/codex-github-operating-system.md` → **Continuation and stop admission**.

An OPEN task with a safe authorized executable next action requires doing it now, not just diagnosing or planning it.

A self-authored scope or completed lease cannot cancel parent implementation authority.

Check the actual final output: stop only at an evidenced boundary,

finish independent work,

and preserve explicit owner restrictions and real access, spending, privacy, platform, and irreversible-action gates.

- execute-open-frontier: final-delivery -> owner-visible-final [semantic; L2]
  Do: Apply stop admission and execute safe authorized work before final delivery.
  Reject: only reading the rule without stop admission; diagnostic summary instead of executable work; child lease completion treated as root completion; a promise to continue later; one blocked dependency used to stop all work; continuation used to bypass a real gate

### uda.kernel.coordination @ r3 (AGENTS.md)

When multiple safe in-scope execution approaches achieve the same outcome, choose the better-coordinated approach without asking the owner to select an execution mode:

use isolated workspaces,

a durable plan and recovery ledger,

delegation plus independent review when safely separable and decision-relevant,

and serialize shared mutable state.

This standing permission does not broaden task authority and does not replace substantive owner decisions.

- choose-coordinated-route: pre-action -> authorized execution boundary [semantic; L2; C]
  Do: Choose the better-coordinated safe route within the same owner outcome.
  Reject: asking the owner to pick a routine execution mode; concurrent writers sharing mutable state; plan present only in disposable chat; delegation presented as its own independent review; parallel writes to the same mutable resource; coordination used to invent additional authority

### uda.kernel.followup-derivation @ r2 (AGENTS.md)

Before authoring, launching, or accepting a consequential follow-up task, re-bind the proposed work to the current parent owner outcome

and follow `patterns/owner-goal-followup-and-requirement-accretion.md`.

First classify the root outcome as `OPEN`, `SATISFIED`, `SUPERSEDED`, `CANCELED`, or `AUTHORITY_UNRESOLVED`,

and state the exact remaining owner gap.

A useful improvement is not unfinished owner work merely because it is technically attractive.

Every new mandatory requirement that was not already present in the owner outcome must declare its origin and necessity.

An `ASSISTANT_INFERENCE` or inherited choice (not a declared gate) with unresolved necessity may be only a bounded reversible experiment; it may not become a fail-closed blocker, architecture prerequisite, root acceptance criterion, stronger assurance gate, or reason to disable a previously working owner-aligned path.

Treat stronger assurance as requirement accretion when it changes whether work may proceed or count as complete.

Independent readback, provider attestation, extra reviewers, new trust boundaries, and similar controls must identify the current owner decision/outcome they materially change and why a simpler evidence standard is insufficient before becoming mandatory.

If a newly added control blocks or degrades a previously working owner-aligned path, stop the compensating-fix chain

and revalidate the first added requirement against the parent outcome and the strongest materially simpler alternative.

Preserve useful supporting work,

but restore the simpler valid path when necessity is not established.

This gate runs at follow-up-task authoring, before the new framing is handed to Work or another executor.

A later worker faithfully executing a substituted goal is too late.

At experiment launch, apply the operational owner-method contract to the actual runnable configuration.

- rebind-before-author-launch-accept: reasoning -> current task decision [semantic; L2; C]
  Do: Admit follow-ups against the current parent outcome and necessary requirements.
  Reject: child goal authored without the parent binding; useful improvement described as an unmet requirement; an attractive improvement promoted to owner-required work; stronger requirement added without origin; unresolved inference promoted to a fail-closed blocker; extra assurance called neutral bookkeeping; extra reviewer required merely because it seems safer; deferring goal review to the executor; worker-to-contract success used to prove owner alignment; naming the follow-up pattern without applying its gate; a proxy improvement substituted for the current owner gap
- revalidate-first-added-control: pre-action -> authorized execution boundary [semantic; L2; C]
  Do: Revalidate the first regressing added control before compensating repairs.
  Reject: repairing around an unvalidated first blocker; keeping the working path disabled while necessity remains unresolved; another compensating fix launched before revalidation; discarding useful support when removing the added blocker
- actual-runnable-method: pre-action -> authorized execution boundary [semantic; L2; C]
  Do: At launch check the owner-method contract against the actual runnable configuration.
  Reject: a second self-authored promise substituted for runnable configuration

### uda.kernel.instruction-activation @ r2 (AGENTS.md)

Before handling any task, including a brief request to remember a preference, open `LESSON-INDEX.md`,

select entries whose triggers match,

and read their current patterns.

activation uses `patterns/task-time-lesson-activation.md`.

Resolve graph-covered dependencies via `rules/UDA-RULE-GRAPH.json`/`scripts/uda_rule_graph.py`;

canonical prose remains authoritative;

unmapped rules stay index-routed;

shopping routes through `LESSON-INDEX.md`.

- open-index-every-task: retrieval -> current reasoning/execution turn [semantic; L2]
  Do: Load the index and current matching patterns under the activation lifecycle.
  Reject: brief task used to skip the index; loading unrelated rules as a substitute for relevant selection; index entries treated as loaded pattern content; a second incompatible activation ledger
- resolve-covered-dependencies: retrieval -> current reasoning/execution turn [semantic; L2]
  Do: Resolve graph-covered dependencies and retain authoritative index/prose routing.
  Reject: hand-selected rule list without declared dependency closure; graph metadata used to override prose; graph absence treated as nonapplicability; a shopping task routed from memory

### uda.kernel.operation-commitments @ r2 (AGENTS.md)

When you explicitly commit to a substantive operation, method, comparison, audit, experiment, or artifact, keep it as an open obligation until it is actually executed, I explicitly supersede it, or new evidence makes it invalid and you say so.

Adjacent analysis, planning, preparation, or a different method does not count as completion.

Before switching methods, declaring progress complete, or ending a substantial pass, verify what observable result proves each promised operation actually occurred.

If a still-valid promised step was displaced by later work, execute it before continuing.

- keep-promised-operation-open: pre-action -> operation-commitment-ledger [semantic; L2; C]
  Do: Keep explicit operation commitments open until their observable result exists.
  Reject: dropping a promised operation from the ledger; adjacent preparation labeled as execution; method switch without checking outstanding commitments; later work silently displacing an outstanding promise

### uda.kernel.operational-references @ r2 (AGENTS.md)

In user-facing prose, never make repository identifiers the primary explanation.

Pull-request numbers, issue numbers, branch names, commit SHAs, workflow/run/job IDs, and similar opaque references are locating metadata, not semantic referents.

- plain-language-first: pre-action -> owner-visible-message [semantic; L2]
  Do: Explain operational objects and relations plainly before locating metadata.
  Reject: opaque identifiers as the primary explanation; bare identifier chain offered as an explanation

### uda.kernel.outbound-links @ r2 (AGENTS.md)

Immediately before surfacing any outbound link to the owner, open the exact destination, follow redirects, and verify that the final page resolves successfully to the intended current content—not an error, 404, dead, parked, or stale page.

Search snippets, cached previews, remembered URLs, and earlier checks do not count as verification.

If the exact link cannot be verified in the current turn, do not surface it.

Never present a broken or unverified link as a recommendation.

- exact-current-destination: pre-action -> owner-visible-message [semantic; L2; C]
  Do: Verify each exact current outbound destination immediately before surfacing it.
  Reject: search snippets used as link verification; remembered URL treated as verified; unverified link surfaced with a caveat; broken link kept as a recommendation

### uda.kernel.output-budget @ r2 (AGENTS.md)

**Every turn:** reusable output over ~8,000 characters goes in a file, for any recipient;

chat gets a summary: `patterns/worker-directive-delivery-and-chat-output-budget.md`.

- file-for-long-reusable-output: handoff -> recipient-file-and-chat-summary [semantic; L2; C]
  Do: Deliver reusable output over ~8,000 characters in a file with a chat summary.
  Reject: long reusable payload pasted into chat; file created without a usable handoff

### uda.kernel.owner-input-continuation @ r3 (AGENTS.md)

An owner answer, correction, upload, or requested clarification is input to the active task, not a completion event.

After incorporating it, continue automatically to the next safe in-scope action while the stated goal remains unfinished.

Do not return only an acknowledgment or ask the owner what to do next when repository state, the task plan, or the request already determines that step.

Pause only for a genuine missing owner decision, new authority, destructive or irreversible risk, unavailable permission or credential, spending, publication, or access, or an explicit request to stop.

- resume-after-input: pre-action -> authorized execution boundary [semantic; L2; C]
  Do: Incorporate owner input and continue the determined safe in-scope action.
  Reject: owner correction acknowledged as task completion; acknowledgment without resumed action; asking the owner what to do next despite a determined frontier; inventing a permission request for routine work

### uda.kernel.owner-interaction @ r2 (AGENTS.md)

Resolve engineering blockers; ask only about a material tradeoff, with plain consequences and a recommendation, or a required human gate.

Minimize owner choice as an execution invariant.

Resolve routine implementation details and already-authorized subordinate actions without asking.

A confirmation for the same destination, data boundary, scope, and consequence remains valid across retries, resumed execution, or an alternate authorized transport path; a failed tool or transport does not consume that approval.

Ask again only if those facts materially change or the platform requires a fresh human gesture.

If owner interaction is genuinely required, finish independent preparation,

consolidate the exact dependent actions into the fewest confirmations permitted,

explain the concrete downside or risk and why the gate is mandatory,

give a recommended default,

and resume automatically after the answer.

- minimize-owner-choice: pre-action -> authorized execution boundary [semantic; L2]
  Do: Resolve engineering details and preserve valid authorization across retries.
  Reject: routine engineering recovery assigned to the owner; routine execution options sent to the owner; reconfirmation of an already-authorized detail; failed transport treated as consuming approval; retry alone used to demand a new confirmation
- consolidate-confirmations: pre-action -> owner-visible-message [semantic; L2; C]
  Do: Prepare a concrete minimal owner question at a genuine decision or human gate.
  Reject: asking before independent preparation is ready; separate routine confirmations for the same gate; an unexplained permission prompt; opaque alternatives without recommendation; cleared gate followed only by acknowledgment

### uda.kernel.target-recovery @ r2 (AGENTS.md)

Before declaring a host, device, service, session, or other target inaccessible—or asking the owner to identify, restart, reconnect, or configure an opaque machine-generated target—recover its semantic identity and the authorized access topology first.

Treat a failed connector/device transport as a route-specific failure, not proof that the underlying target is unavailable.

Inspect current connected endpoints plus task-relevant local mappings such as SSH config/aliases, durable task state, service/process metadata, and recent authorized execution history;

from a healthy authorized endpoint, use bounded read-only probes such as `hostname` and exact target-path existence/read checks to prove which route reaches the same target.

Use an equivalent authorized alternate route when one exists.

Never ask the owner to recognize an opaque identifier merely because the first transport failed.

Escalate only after plausible authorized routes are exhausted or a genuinely human-only action remains.

- identity-and-topology-before-escalation: pre-action -> owner-visible-message [semantic; L2; C]
  Do: Recover target identity and authorized routes before an accessibility claim or request.
  Reject: opaque target handed to the owner after one failure; one route failure called target unavailability; unavailability claim without topology probes; available alternate route ignored; asking the owner to identify an opaque handle; escalation after only the first failed route; route equivalence assumed without exact-resource probes

### uda.kernel.work-permissions @ r2 (AGENTS.md)

Work selects authorized task-scoped access and the automatic reviewer; do not ask the owner to choose routine permissions.

This adds no semantic, spending, publication, representation, destructive, or self-approval authority.

- automatic-task-access-review: pre-action -> authorized execution boundary [semantic; L2]
  Do: Work selects authorized task access and automatic review without routine permission questions.
  Reject: asking the owner to choose routine permissions; automatic review treated as self-approval authority

## Shared lifecycle
L1: Carry: Open obligations remain active across handoff, rewrite, and compaction until satisfied or superseded. Repair: Recompile the active contract with the missing boundary binding.
L2: Carry: Retain this boundary and evidence across handoffs, compaction and rewrites; recheck changed inputs. Repair: Perform the required behavior at its due boundary and bind a fresh receipt to the repaired candidate.
L3: Carry: Execution receipts return facts; subsequent consequential reasoning returns to Chat. Repair: Move substantive reasoning back to Chat and reduce the worker directive to bounded execution.
L4: Carry: A subtask completion does not close the parent outcome. Repair: Resume the next safe authorized action before finalizing.
L5: Carry: Keep saving at each completed step across turns, compaction, model changes and account switches; carry the current goal, constraints and remaining action into the successor checkpoint. Repair: The worker holding the context saves and pushes the completed work and repairs done, next and the exact next action before continuing; preserve and name any real access or publication gate.
L6: Carry: Recheck the durable handoff after any change in this turn's state or final rewrite; private state and account-bound recreation duties travel with the one-line resume instruction. Repair: Refresh the actual durable checkpoint before final delivery, save private supervisor state through an authorized reachable private route, and add the one-line resume instruction and account-bound recreation list without exposing private data.
L7: Carry: Retain this boundary and evidence across handoffs, compaction and rewrites; recheck changed inputs. Repair: Prepend the required timestamp; rerun the first-line check.

For **every assistant turn** governed by this architecture, the **first line of the final user-visible assistant answer MUST be an explicit date-and-time stamp including a timezone or UTC offset**.

This is a final-output contract and a pre-answer invariant, not a task-dependent recommendation.

The timestamp must appear in the final answer/message content delivered to the user on every assistant turn.

A timestamp written only in hidden reasoning, visible thinking/reasoning UI, analysis, tool-call commentary, scratch work, or any intermediate channel **does not satisfy this requirement**.

An earlier timestamp in reasoning or an intermediate step does not satisfy the final-output contract; use the second reading in the final answer.

The final answer opens with the second reading

and says how long the turn took in total.

Before finalizing every assistant turn, perform a literal output check: the first user-visible line of the final answer must match a date + time + timezone/UTC-offset form.

If it does not, prepend the second reading; the check needs no further reading.

Apply it on every turn even for trivial arithmetic, greetings, smoke tests, follow-up acknowledgments, corrections, status updates, or prompts that otherwise warrant a direct one-line answer.

Simple answers, low-effort reasoning, tool avoidance, brevity, and shallow repository reads **must not waive this invariant**.

Treat failure to emit the timestamp as the first line of the final user-visible answer on any assistant turn as an instruction-following failure even when the timestamp appeared during thinking or the underlying task answer is otherwise correct.

Two clock readings per turn, no others (owner, 2026-09-30).

First: the message's sent time if the surface shows it, else a read as the turn's first action.

Second: a read right before writing the final answer.

Read with `date -u` in a shell tool, else the current-time tool, else the code tool's clock;

if a read fails or isn't later than the first, use the next one once.

Never compare clocks or read mid-task.

Don't reuse a prior-turn timestamp

or present capture time as hidden provider sent time.

If no clock answers, say so rather than inventing a time.

Before authoring, launching, or accepting a consequential follow-up task, re-bind the proposed work to the current parent owner outcome

and follow `patterns/owner-goal-followup-and-requirement-accretion.md`.

First classify the root outcome as `OPEN`, `SATISFIED`, `SUPERSEDED`, `CANCELED`, or `AUTHORITY_UNRESOLVED`,

and state the exact remaining owner gap.

A useful improvement is not unfinished owner work merely because it is technically attractive.

Every new mandatory requirement that was not already present in the owner outcome must declare its origin and necessity.

An `ASSISTANT_INFERENCE` or inherited choice (not a declared gate) with unresolved necessity may be only a bounded reversible experiment; it may not become a fail-closed blocker, architecture prerequisite, root acceptance criterion, stronger assurance gate, or reason to disable a previously working owner-aligned path.

Treat stronger assurance as requirement accretion when it changes whether work may proceed or count as complete.

Independent readback, provider attestation, extra reviewers, new trust boundaries, and similar controls must identify the current owner decision/outcome they materially change and why a simpler evidence standard is insufficient before becoming mandatory.

If a newly added control blocks or degrades a previously working owner-aligned path, stop the compensating-fix chain

and revalidate the first added requirement against the parent outcome and the strongest materially simpler alternative.

Preserve useful supporting work,

but restore the simpler valid path when necessity is not established.

This gate runs at follow-up-task authoring, before the new framing is handed to Work or another executor.

A later worker faithfully executing a substituted goal is too late.

At experiment launch, apply the operational owner-method contract to the actual runnable configuration.

Before declaring a host, device, service, session, or other target inaccessible—or asking the owner to identify, restart, reconnect, or configure an opaque machine-generated target—recover its semantic identity and the authorized access topology first.

Inspect current connected endpoints plus task-relevant local mappings such as SSH config/aliases, durable task state, service/process metadata, and recent authorized execution history;

from a healthy authorized endpoint, use bounded read-only probes such as `hostname` and exact target-path existence/read checks to prove which route reaches the same target.

Use an equivalent authorized alternate route when one exists.

Never ask the owner to recognize an opaque identifier merely because the first transport failed.

Escalate only after plausible authorized routes are exhausted or a genuinely human-only action remains.
